nodes.title: Online reviews can predict long-term returns of individual stocks

nodes.name: consumer sentiment underreaction
nodes.description: Negative consumer sentiment expressed in online reviews contains predictive information about future firm fundamentals (revenue, earnings, cash flow) that is not immediately incorporated into stock prices, allowing investors to exploit the delayed market reaction to this sentiment signal.

nodes.name: fundamental cash flow forecasting via consumer feedback
nodes.description: Aggregated consumer reviews provide a real-time, granular signal of customer satisfaction and purchasing intent that predicts future corporate cash flows and sales more accurately than traditional financial metrics, enabling long-term return prediction.

nodes.title: The Impact of Customer Online Satisfaction on Stock Returns: Evidence from the E-commerce Reviews in China

nodes.name: fundamental surprise prediction
nodes.description: Customer negative sentiment tendency predicts future revenue surprises, earnings surprises, and cash flow shocks, indicating that consumer reviews reveal early signals of deteriorating firm fundamentals before they are officially reported.

nodes.name: information asymmetry exploitation
nodes.description: The predictive power of consumer sentiment is strongest in growth companies and firms with lower accounting transparency, where traditional financial disclosures are less informative, allowing consumer reviews to fill the information gap and drive returns.

nodes.title: A Rational Finance Explanation of the Stock Predictability Puzzle

nodes.name: asymmetric information between option and spot traders
nodes.description: Option traders possess superior predictability of stock returns relative to spot traders, particularly when options are deep in or out of the money. This information asymmetry allows option traders to price derivatives more accurately, creating exploitable mispricings in the options market.

nodes.name: moneyness-dependent predictability differential
nodes.description: The predictability of stock returns incorporated into option prices varies monotonically with moneyness: option traders' predictability advantage increases with moneyness extremity (deep ITM/OTM), while spot traders' predictability decreases. At-the-money options show equal predictability between trader types.

nodes.name: variance risk premium as return predictor
nodes.description: The spread between implied variance (from option prices) and realized variance contains predictive information about future stock returns. This premium reflects option traders' superior ability to forecast volatility and returns relative to spot market consensus.

nodes.title: A Study on Neural Network Architecture Applied to the Prediction of Brazilian Stock Returns
Supervised Neural Networks for Illiquid Alternative Asset Cash Flow Forecasting

nodes.name: J-curve timing prediction
nodes.description: Private equity funds exhibit a characteristic J-curve pattern where early cash outflows (contributions) precede later cash inflows (distributions). Superior forecasting of the timing and magnitude of these cash flows allows institutional investors to optimize fund allocation decisions and capture returns by better anticipating liquidity events.

nodes.name: macroeconomic state-dependent cash flow sensitivity
nodes.description: Private equity fund cash flows are sensitive to macroeconomic conditions; integrating macroeconomic indicators into forecasting models improves prediction accuracy by capturing how market environment (economic cycles, credit conditions, etc.) affects the timing and size of contributions and distributions.

nodes.title: Earnings Prediction with Deep Learning

nodes.name: analyst forecast error exploitation
nodes.description: Machine learning models produce more accurate earnings forecasts than sell-side analysts, allowing traders to profit from the market's reliance on inferior analyst estimates. As the market gradually incorporates the superior ML-generated forecasts, prices drift toward fundamental values.

nodes.name: earnings surprise underreaction
nodes.description: Markets underreact to new, unexpected earnings information because traditional analyst forecasts are biased or incomplete. Superior earnings predictions reveal surprises that the market has not yet fully priced in, allowing investors to profit from subsequent price adjustments.

nodes.title: Stock returns versus trading volume: is the correspondence more general?

nodes.name: square-root price impact of volume
nodes.description: Trade volume impacts prices with a square-root relationship (r(V) ∝ V^(1/2)), creating predictable price movements based on volume magnitude. This systematic relationship allows traders to anticipate price changes by observing volume changes.

nodes.name: power-law scaling of returns and volume distributions
nodes.description: Both stock returns and trading volumes follow power-law distributions with scaling exponents systematically related by a factor of ~2 (return exponents larger than volume exponents). This consistent scaling relationship across stocks enables volume-based return prediction.

nodes.title: Forecasting stock market returns over multiple time horizons

nodes.name: news-driven nonlinear feedback on longer horizons
nodes.description: News impacts stock returns nonlinearly and persists over longer timescales (days to months) through feedback mechanisms, creating predictable return patterns that markets fail to efficiently price. This contrasts with rapid intraday adjustment, where markets are nearly efficient.

nodes.name: market microstructure efficiency differential across timescales
nodes.description: Stock markets exhibit near-efficiency on intraday timescales where news is quickly incorporated, but become inefficient on longer timescales where the same news has delayed and nonlinear effects, enabling predictability and alpha generation on multi-day to multi-month horizons.

nodes.name: heterogeneous investor horizon-driven market transitions
nodes.description: The presence of investors with different investment horizons creates transitions between bull and bear markets and generates self-similar price behavior across multiple timescales, enabling predictable market regime shifts.

nodes.title: Multi-Horizon Echo State Network Prediction of Intraday Stock Returns

nodes.name: temporal pattern exploitation via recurrent dynamics
nodes.description: Intraday stock returns exhibit exploitable temporal dependencies and sequential patterns that can be captured through recurrent neural network architectures. By modeling the temporal dynamics of market data, the ESN identifies these patterns to predict future returns at multiple horizons.

nodes.title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models

nodes.name: underreaction to negative news
nodes.description: Markets fail to immediately incorporate negative information from news headlines into prices, leaving a drift opportunity. LLMs can identify this mispricings by processing news semantics more effectively than the marginal market participant.

nodes.name: information-processing capacity constraints
nodes.description: Market participants have limited cognitive and computational capacity to process complex news signals, especially in small stocks. LLMs with superior language understanding can extract predictive signals that human traders and simpler algorithms miss.

nodes.name: limits to arbitrage in small stocks
nodes.description: Small stocks have higher trading costs, lower liquidity, and less analyst coverage, preventing rapid arbitrage correction of LLM-identified mispricings. This allows the predictive advantage to persist longer before being competed away.

nodes.title: Autonomous Market Intelligence: Agentic AI Nowcasting Predicts Stock Returns

nodes.name: information synthesis advantage
nodes.description: AI systems can synthesize diverse real-time web information more effectively than market participants, identifying genuine positive signals that are coherent and actionable. This creates a predictability edge in top-ranked stocks where positive news generates clear, non-noisy signals.

nodes.name: asymmetric information noise filtering
nodes.description: Positive news generates coherent, detectable signals while negative news is contaminated by strategic corporate obfuscation and social media noise, making AI selection ability asymmetric—strong for identifying winners but ineffective for identifying losers.

nodes.name: liquidity-constrained alpha concentration
nodes.description: Alpha generation is concentrated in highly liquid Russell 1000 stocks where transaction costs are minimized (less than 10% of gross alpha), allowing the information advantage to translate into implementable returns. This concentration reflects both the AI's selection ability and market microstructure constraints.

nodes.title: Designing an Optimal Portfolio for Iran's Stock Market with Genetic Algorithm using Neural Network Prediction of Risk and Return Stocks

nodes.name: neural network return prediction alpha
nodes.description: A neural network trained on historical stock data predicts future returns, allowing identification of mispriced assets. By allocating capital to stocks with favorable predicted returns, the portfolio captures alpha from the model's ability to forecast price movements.

nodes.name: prediction error risk assessment
nodes.description: The magnitude of prediction errors from the neural network serves as a measure of stock-specific risk. Stocks with larger prediction errors are treated as riskier, allowing the portfolio to adjust allocations based on model uncertainty rather than just historical volatility.

nodes.title: Fat Tails in Financial Return Distributions Revisited: Evidence from the Korean Stock Market

nodes.name: fat-tail mispricing in small-cap stocks
nodes.description: Small-capitalization stocks exhibit persistent fat tails in their return distributions that are not explained by market crashes or volatility clustering. Traders can exploit mispriced tail risk by positioning for the higher likelihood of extreme price movements in these stocks during periods of volatility.

nodes.name: volatility clustering underestimation
nodes.description: Standard volatility clustering models (GARCH) fail to fully capture the fat-tail behavior in small-cap stock returns, leaving residual tail risk that can be exploited. The persistence of fat tails after GARCH filtering indicates that conditional volatility models underestimate tail risk.

nodes.title: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models for Stock Return Prediction Using Newsflow

nodes.name: sentiment signal extraction from newsflow
nodes.description: Fine-tuned LLMs extract nuanced market sentiment and information content from financial news articles more accurately than traditional sentiment analysis, generating predictive signals for stock returns.

nodes.name: token-level embedding aggregation for return forecasting
nodes.description: Aggregating token-level embeddings from LLM representations (rather than document-level representations) captures granular linguistic patterns in financial news that improve stock return prediction accuracy.

nodes.title: One Factor to Bind the Cross-Section of Returns

nodes.name: nonlinear factor loading interaction
nodes.description: Asset returns respond nonlinearly to a single latent factor through heterogeneous, time-dependent factor loadings. This nonlinear relationship captures complex interactions that linear multi-factor models miss, generating alpha by more accurately pricing cross-sectional return variation.

nodes.title: Michael Milken: The Junk Dealer

nodes.name: junk bond mispricing exploitation
nodes.description: High-yield bonds issued by low-profile, high-risk companies are systematically undervalued by the market due to information asymmetry and risk aversion. Thorough fundamental research identifies genuinely viable firms whose credit risk is overpriced, allowing investors to earn alpha by holding diversified portfolios of these mispriced securities.

nodes.name: research-driven risk mitigation
nodes.description: Systematic, deep fundamental analysis of high-risk companies reduces actual default risk relative to market-implied risk premia. This allows portfolio construction that achieves high returns while maintaining acceptable risk levels through diversification across thoroughly-researched positions.

nodes.title: Zero-Coupon Treasury Rates and Returns using the Volatility Index

nodes.name: equity volatility spillover to bond pricing
nodes.description: Stock market volatility (VIX) contains predictive information about Treasury bond rate movements across the yield curve. This cross-asset volatility signal allows more accurate forecasting of bond returns than models that treat Treasury volatility in isolation.

nodes.name: bond mispricing convergence
nodes.description: The VIX-informed model identifies Treasury bonds trading away from their fair values implied by the volatility-adjusted term structure. Alpha is generated by exploiting the predictable convergence of mispriced bonds back to fair value.

nodes.title: Trading-profit attribution for the size factor

nodes.name: rebalancing-induced size factor capture
nodes.description: Equal-weighted portfolio rebalancing mechanically forces systematic buying of smaller positions (which have underperformed) and selling of larger positions (which have outperformed), thereby capturing the size factor premium through disciplined mean-reversion trading rather than fundamental insight.

nodes.name: rebalancing-drift alpha generation
nodes.description: The systematic rebalancing trades embedded in equal-weighted portfolio maintenance generate alpha by exploiting the lag between price movements and the rebalancing trigger, allowing the strategy to profit from predictable mean-reverting flows.

nodes.title: Parameters of Profitability: Evidence From Conventional and Islamic Banks of Bangladesh

nodes.name: Islamic bank outperformance in declining profitability regime
nodes.description: Islamic banks maintain superior ROA relative to conventional banks during periods of declining average banking sector profitability, suggesting structural advantages in cost management or asset quality that persist when conventional banks face headwinds.

nodes.name: bank-specific factor heterogeneity in profitability
nodes.description: Bank-specific operational and balance-sheet factors (e.g., capital adequacy, asset composition, cost efficiency) are significant drivers of ROA variation across banks, creating persistent performance differences exploitable through fundamental analysis.

nodes.title: The Returns to Science in the Presence of Technological Risk

nodes.name: technological risk mispricing
nodes.description: Markets misprice assets exposed to scientific advancement by underweighting tail risks from catastrophic technological events (e.g., engineered pandemics). Investors can exploit this by using expert forecasts of existential risk to identify undervalued or overvalued sectors.

nodes.name: scientific progress value discrepancy
nodes.description: Market participants disagree on or systematically misprice the expected social returns to scientific advancement when incorporating both productivity benefits and catastrophic downside risks. This creates alpha opportunities by correctly weighting expert forecasts of both benefits and tail risks.

nodes.title: Wax and wane of the cross-sectional momentum and contrarian effects: Evidence from the Chinese stock markets

nodes.name: market trend-dependent reversal profitability
nodes.description: Contrarian strategy profitability varies with market trend direction; upward market trends create conditions where mean reversion is more profitable, suggesting that investor overreaction and subsequent correction intensity depend on whether the market is in an uptrend or downtrend.

nodes.name: volatility-dependent reversal profitability
nodes.description: Higher market volatility strengthens contrarian strategy returns, implying that periods of elevated price dispersion create stronger mean-reversion opportunities as investors overreact more dramatically during volatile regimes.

nodes.name: liquidity-dependent reversal profitability
nodes.description: Contrarian profitability increases when market liquidity is higher, suggesting that better liquidity enables more efficient execution of mean-reversion trades and may indicate that liquidity provision reduces the friction preventing arbitrage of overreaction.

nodes.name: macroeconomic uncertainty-dependent reversal profitability
nodes.description: Lower macroeconomic uncertainty strengthens contrarian strategy returns, implying that when macro uncertainty is high, investors become more risk-averse and less willing to arbitrage mispricings, reducing mean-reversion opportunities.

nodes.title: 4-Factor Model for Overnight Returns

nodes.name: intraday momentum exhaustion
nodes.description: Intraday momentum signals derived from price and volume patterns lose predictive power or reverse by the overnight horizon, as short-term directional pressure dissipates without fundamental support.

nodes.name: intraday liquidity-driven pricing
nodes.description: Intraday volume patterns and liquidity conditions create temporary price deviations that are not sustained overnight, as liquidity-driven trading pressure reverses when market participants exit positions.

nodes.title: Profit warnings and stock returns: Evidence from moroccan stock exchange

nodes.name: qualitative warning overreaction
nodes.description: Markets overreact to qualitative profit warnings (vague, non-numeric disclosures) relative to quantitative warnings, generating larger negative abnormal returns that subsequently reverse, allowing profitable short positions.

nodes.name: information precision discount
nodes.description: Investors penalize qualitative (low-precision) profit warnings more severely than quantitative (high-precision) warnings because qualitative information is harder to interpret and triggers greater uncertainty, leading to differential price impacts.

nodes.title: A Study on Impact of Capital Structure on Profitability of Companies Listed in Indian Stock Exchange with respect to Automobile Industry

nodes.name: capital structure efficiency premium
nodes.description: Firms with optimal debt-to-equity ratios achieve higher profitability (RoCE, RoNW) because they balance financial leverage benefits against distress costs, allowing better capital allocation and sustained returns on invested capital.

nodes.name: financial obligation sustainability
nodes.description: Companies with stronger interest coverage ratios and balanced capital structures are better positioned to meet debt obligations and fund growth investments, reducing default risk and enabling consistent profitability.

nodes.title: On statistical arbitrage under a conditional factor model of equity returns

nodes.name: mean reversion from latent factor mispricing
nodes.description: Assets deviate from their expected returns as predicted by time-varying latent risk factors; these deviations represent temporary mispricings that revert to the conditional factor model's predictions, generating alpha when the model correctly identifies the latent factor structure.

nodes.name: time-varying risk premium capture
nodes.description: Risk premia on systematic factors are non-stationary and change over time; a state-space model that filters and updates estimates of these time-varying premia can exploit periods when the market has not yet repriced assets for shifts in factor risk compensation.

nodes.title: A Spectral Generalisation of the Variance Ratio: Eigenstructure of Long-Horizon Portfolio Covariance and a Multi-Memory Factor Model of U.S. Equity Returns

nodes.name: return-channel long memory
nodes.description: Equity returns exhibit persistent autocorrelation at long horizons driven by a distinct cross-sectional loading structure, enabling predictability of future returns from past return patterns independent of volatility dynamics.

nodes.name: volatility-channel cascade memory
nodes.description: Volatility exhibits multi-scale persistent memory with a regime transition in the late 1980s, where the slowest volatility component lengthened from ~2 to ~4 years, creating exploitable long-horizon volatility predictability distinct from return predictability.

nodes.name: cross-channel loading anti-alignment
nodes.description: Characteristics that predict return momentum patterns are economically distinct from and negatively aligned with those predicting volatility persistence, meaning assets with strong return memory do not necessarily exhibit strong volatility memory, enabling separate factor-based exploitation.

nodes.title: Uncovering a factor-based expected return conditioning structure with Regression Trees jointly for many stocks

nodes.name: non-linear factor interaction pricing
nodes.description: Stock returns exhibit non-linear dependencies with the three-factor model that linear regression overlooks. Regression trees capture these complex interactions and conditional relationships among factors, enabling more accurate expected return predictions than traditional linear models.

nodes.name: market factor dominance in return conditioning
nodes.description: The market excess return factor is consistently the most informative variable for conditioning expected returns across multiple stocks, suggesting that market-relative dynamics drive return predictability more than size or value factors in a non-linear framework.

nodes.title: Identifying and Estimating Perceived Returns to Binary Investments

nodes.name: perceived return misestimation
nodes.description: Agents systematically misperceive returns to binary investments due to imperfect knowledge of prices and structural parameters. Traders can exploit the gap between agents' perceived returns and actual returns by using price variation that is known to agents.

nodes.name: price misperception from agent knowledge gaps
nodes.description: Agents have imperfect knowledge of prices and cannot accurately infer structural relationships between profits, revenues, and costs, leading to systematic mispricings. This creates exploitable discrepancies when price variations are observable to agents but uncorrelated with their unobserved misperceptions.

nodes.title: Comprehensive Analysis On Determinants Of Bank Profitability In Bangladesh
Business Model Contributions to Bank Profit Performance: A Machine Learning Approach

nodes.name: business model profitability differentiation
nodes.description: Retail-oriented bank business models generate superior risk-adjusted returns compared to non-specialized models due to more efficient balance sheet composition and operational focus. Investors can exploit this by systematically identifying and favoring retail-specialized banks based on their balance sheet structure.

nodes.name: capital ratio efficiency heterogeneity
nodes.description: The relationship between capital ratios and profitability is not uniform across business models; retail-oriented banks extract greater returns from capital holdings than non-specialized banks. This suggests capital efficiency varies systematically with business model choice.

nodes.name: crisis-driven profitability degradation
nodes.description: Macroeconomic shocks (Great Recession) reduce the profitability contributions of all business models, with incomplete recovery in post-crisis periods. This suggests structural changes in banking economics persist beyond crisis resolution.

nodes.title: FactorGCL: A Hypergraph-Based Factor Model with Temporal Residual Contrastive Learning for Stock Returns Prediction

nodes.name: hidden factor extraction from residuals
nodes.description: Stock returns contain systematic information beyond traditional linear factors. By extracting factors from the residuals of prior factor models (cascading residual architecture), the model captures high-order nonlinear relationships that are less noisy and better reflect underlying return dynamics, improving predictive accuracy.

nodes.name: temporal residual consistency
nodes.description: Stock-specific residual patterns exhibit temporal persistence. By contrasting residual information across different time periods, the model identifies which hidden factors are stable and economically meaningful rather than noise, thereby improving the signal-to-noise ratio in factor extraction.

nodes.title: The Micro-Aggregated Profit Share

nodes.name: market power markup mispricing
nodes.description: Firms with increasing market power can sustain higher markups and greater profitability, but traditional valuation metrics fail to fully price in these shifts in market power dynamics, creating mispricings that can be exploited.

nodes.name: returns-to-scale profitability leverage
nodes.description: Firms operating with increasing returns to scale can achieve higher profitability per unit of output; those that effectively leverage their production network position outperform when markets misprice this efficiency advantage.

nodes.title: Stochastic Discount Factors with Cross-Asset Spillovers

nodes.name: cross-asset information spillover
nodes.description: Large, low-turnover firms transmit predictive information to other assets through an information network. Price movements and characteristics in these net-transmitter firms causally influence expected returns of connected assets.

nodes.name: firm-level characteristic predictability
nodes.description: Firm-specific characteristics (e.g., size, turnover, valuation metrics) have directional predictive power for future returns. These signals are jointly estimated with spillover effects to improve out-of-sample return forecasting.

nodes.name: SDF-based mispricing correction
nodes.description: The stochastic discount factor derived from unified firm signals and spillovers identifies systematic mispricings by ranking the relevance of asset characteristics. Assets with SDF-implied discount rates diverging from market prices generate alpha through mean reversion.

nodes.title: A Study on Impact of Environmental Accounting on Profitability of Companies listed in Bombay Stock Exchange

nodes.name: environmental responsibility undervaluation
nodes.description: Markets underprice firms that invest in environmental protection despite these investments generating measurable improvements in profitability metrics (ROCE, ROA, ROE, net margins). Investors fail to recognize that environmental accounting expenditures correlate with superior long-term returns.

nodes.title: Factorising equity returns in an emerging market through exogenous shocks and capital flows

nodes.name: capital distribution rebalancing
nodes.description: Returns are driven by shifts in how capital is allocated across stocks within a portfolio. As capital concentrates in or flows away from certain holdings, portfolio returns are mechanically affected by the reweighting of positions, independent of individual stock performance.

nodes.name: stock rank momentum effect
nodes.description: Changes in the relative ranking of stocks by size or performance within a portfolio generate returns. Stocks that rise in rank (relative outperformers) contribute positive returns, while those that fall in rank contribute negative returns, creating a momentum-like signal from rank transitions.

nodes.name: capital flow risk premium
nodes.description: Equity returns in emerging markets are driven by net capital flows (foreign direct investment and portfolio investment) acting as a systematic risk factor. Periods of capital inflow/outflow create return patterns that are distinct from and complementary to traditional macroeconomic risk factors.

nodes.title: A Modeling Approach of Return and Volatility of Structured Investment Products with Caps and Floors

nodes.name: principal protection underperformance
nodes.description: Structured products with embedded caps and floors (principal protection features) mechanically underperform direct stock market exposure because the floor constraint truncates upside returns while the cap limits gains, creating a drag on expected returns relative to unconstrained equity investment.

nodes.name: risk-return profile mismatch
nodes.description: Structured products with caps and floors exhibit a poor risk-return tradeoff where investors bear substantial volatility (nearly 2x that of bonds) while earning returns only marginally above risk-free instruments, failing to adequately compensate for the embedded tail risk and convexity costs.

nodes.title: Embedding-based neural network for investment return prediction

nodes.name: nonlinear feature interaction capture
nodes.description: Deep learning models capture complex nonlinear relationships and interactions between investment features that traditional machine learning methods (XGBoost, LightGBM) fail to exploit, enabling more accurate return predictions.

nodes.name: embedding-based dimensionality reduction
nodes.description: Encoding investment identifiers into low-dimensional dense vectors maps high-dimensional feature spaces onto a lower-dimensional manifold, allowing competitive representation of complex investment characteristics while reducing noise and improving generalization.

nodes.title: Beyond Prompting: An Autonomous Framework for Systematic Factor Investing via Agentic AI
Anomalous Returns in a Neural Network Equity-Ranking Predictor

nodes.name: nonlinear mean reversion in price-earnings dynamics
nodes.description: Neural networks capture non-linear patterns in the joint dynamics of historical price and earnings changes that linear models miss, enabling superior prediction of quarterly price reversals. This generates alpha by exploiting mean-reverting relationships that traditional ranking systems fail to identify.

nodes.name: earnings surprise momentum interaction
nodes.description: The model's use of both price and earnings percentage changes as inputs suggests it exploits the interaction between earnings surprises and price momentum—specifically, how non-linear combinations of recent earnings and price trends predict subsequent reversals or continuations that simple linear models cannot capture.

nodes.title: Impact of Investing Characteristics on Financial Performance of Individual Investors: An Exploratory Study

nodes.name: behavioral discipline premium
nodes.description: Investors with emotional stability and disciplined decision-making avoid panic selling and overtrading, generating excess returns by maintaining rational portfolio decisions during market stress.

nodes.name: value investing discipline
nodes.description: Investors focusing on intrinsic value and price-independent evaluation generate alpha by avoiding momentum-driven decisions and maintaining positions in undervalued securities regardless of short-term price movements.

nodes.name: time horizon commitment
nodes.description: Investors with middle/long time horizons reduce transaction costs and avoid short-term noise trading, allowing them to capture fundamental returns while avoiding whipsaw losses from mean-reversion.

nodes.title: Invest or Exit? Optimal Decisions in the Face of a Declining Profit Stream

nodes.name: threshold-based investment timing under profit volatility
nodes.description: Firms optimally time investments in aging projects by monitoring profit stream volatility and drift; higher volatility can lower the investment threshold when the profit boost is sufficiently large, allowing firms to invest countercyclically during volatile periods to capture mean reversion.

nodes.name: threshold-based exit timing under declining profits
nodes.description: Firms maintain separate exit thresholds before and after investment; as profit streams deteriorate with negative drift, firms rationally delay exit when volatility is high (preserving the option value of recovery), but exit when profits fall below a critical threshold that makes continuation uneconomical.

nodes.title: Equity Default Clawback Swaps to Implement Venture Banking

nodes.name: leverage amplification via default swap hedging
nodes.description: A venture bank uses equity default swaps (EDS) to hedge downside risk on venture loans, allowing it to safely amplify its capital base by 47x or more without central bank funding. The hedging removes tail risk, enabling aggressive leverage that would otherwise be constrained by capital requirements.

nodes.name: clawback lien risk mitigation
nodes.description: A clawback provision (optimized at 77%) is embedded in equity default clawback swaps (EDCS) to eliminate moral hazard—the underwriter's incentive to deliberately cause default to trigger the swap payout. The clawback forces repayment of gains, aligning incentives between the venture bank and swap underwriter.

nodes.name: term-matching of investment and insurance
nodes.description: By matching the maturity of the equity default swap to the maturity of the underlying venture loan, the venture bank eliminates duration mismatch risk that has historically plagued banking. This structural alignment reduces refinancing and rollover risk.

nodes.title: Fair profit sharing ratios of Islamic investment contracts

nodes.name: incentive alignment through equitable profit sharing
nodes.description: Fair allocation of profits based on actual capital and labor contributions aligns incentives among partners, reducing agency conflicts and leading to better investment decisions and enhanced venture performance.

nodes.name: risk-adjusted contribution weighting
nodes.description: Profit shares are determined by weighting each partner's capital and labor contributions by economic factors (investment risk and opportunity cost), ensuring compensation reflects the true economic burden and opportunity cost borne by each party.

nodes.title: ChatGPT in Systematic Investing -- Enhancing Risk-Adjusted Returns with LLMs

nodes.name: news sentiment momentum continuation
nodes.description: LLM-extracted sentiment from firm-specific news predicts whether past momentum will continue, allowing investors to selectively enter momentum positions when news supports trend persistence rather than blindly following price momentum.

nodes.name: selective momentum portfolio construction
nodes.description: By conditioning both stock selection and portfolio weights on LLM-scored news sentiment alignment with past returns, the strategy concentrates capital in high-conviction momentum trades where news fundamentals support continuation, reducing exposure to momentum reversals.

nodes.title: Solution to the Equity Premium Puzzle Using the Sufficiency Factor of the Model

nodes.name: risk aversion mismatch correction
nodes.description: Market prices equities with an implicit risk aversion coefficient that deviates from the theoretically justified level (1.033526). Exploiting this mismatch by aligning pricing with true investor risk preferences generates alpha through correction of systematic mispricings.

nodes.title: On the martingale-fair index of return for investment funds

nodes.name: martingale mispricing detection
nodes.description: Investment funds that deviate from the martingale property (i.e., their returns are not consistent with arbitrage-free pricing) are mispriced. Identifying these deviations allows investors to exploit the discrepancy between observed fund returns and their theoretically fair martingale-consistent returns.

nodes.title: Determinants of Profitability of Banks: Evidence from Islamic Banks of Bangladesh
Strategic mean-variance investing under mean-reverting stock returns

nodes.name: mean-reversion alpha extraction
nodes.description: Stock returns exhibit mean-reversion over the investment horizon, creating favorable risk-reward trade-offs that allow strategic time-dependent allocation to stocks and bonds to generate alpha by exploiting predictable reversions to long-term levels.

nodes.name: portfolio value lower-bound protection
nodes.description: By optimally allocating between mean-reverting stocks and bonds over a specified horizon, the portfolio's terminal value becomes effectively bounded from below, providing a guaranteed minimum return floor with stochastic excess returns above it.

nodes.title: Profitability Analysis in Stock Investment Using an LSTM-Based Deep Learning Model
Equity Tail Risk in the Treasury Bond Market

nodes.name: flight-to-safety demand surge
nodes.description: When equity tail risk (left-tail volatility) increases, investors shift demand toward safe-haven Treasury bonds, driving up bond prices and generating predictable excess returns. This is a flight-to-safety phenomenon where perceived tail risk in equities mechanically increases demand for government bonds.

nodes.name: tail risk premium pricing
nodes.description: Equity tail risk is a priced factor in the Treasury bond market. The term structure of interest rates incorporates compensation for exposure to equity tail risk, such that bonds with greater sensitivity to tail risk shocks command different yields.

nodes.title: The Evolving Causal Structure of Equity Risk Factors

nodes.name: risk contagion through causal factor densification
nodes.description: During financial stress, the causal network among equity risk factors becomes denser, with the market factor's out-degree increasing sharply. This densification causes exposures across nominally diversified factors to converge toward common market risk, amplifying contagion and reducing effective diversification when it is most needed.

nodes.name: factor redundancy and correlation breakdown
nodes.description: Multi-factor portfolios contain significant redundancy among factors, and traditional correlation-based diversification fails during crises because causal relationships—not just correlations—drive factor co-movements. Causal structure analysis reveals hidden dependencies that correlation matrices miss, especially during market turmoil.

nodes.name: dynamic causal rebalancing alpha
nodes.description: Investors can generate alpha by dynamically adjusting multi-factor portfolio weights based on the identified causal structure of risk factors, which evolves over time. By rebalancing in response to changing causal relationships rather than static correlations, portfolios can better mitigate risk contagion and enhance diversification during periods of financial stress.

nodes.title: Minimal Investment Risk with Cost and Return Constraints: A Replica Analysis

nodes.name: heterogeneous transaction cost adjustment
nodes.description: Alpha is generated by accounting for distinct per-unit purchase costs across assets when optimizing portfolio allocation. Traditional models assume uniform costs, but heterogeneous costs cause mispricings that can be exploited through cost-aware reallocation.

nodes.name: fund-size-dependent allocation efficiency
nodes.description: Optimal portfolio allocations vary with the size of investable funds, but standard optimization ignores this dependency. Exploiting the correct fund-size-contingent allocation generates alpha by avoiding the inefficiencies of one-size-fits-all solutions.

nodes.name: constrained risk minimization with return targets
nodes.description: By jointly optimizing for minimum investment risk while satisfying explicit cost and return constraints (rather than treating them separately), the model identifies allocations that traditional unconstrained approaches miss, generating outperformance.

nodes.title: The joint distribution of stock returns is not elliptical

nodes.name: elliptical model mispricing
nodes.description: Traditional elliptical models (including Student copulas) systematically misprice pairs of stocks with lower linear correlations because they assume a single volatility mode across all stocks, failing to capture the true joint distribution of returns. Traders can exploit this mispricing by using non-elliptical copulas that better account for varying volatility structures.

nodes.name: volatility heterogeneity across stock pairs
nodes.description: The joint distribution of stock returns exhibits varying volatility regimes that depend on the correlation structure between pairs; elliptical models fail because they impose homogeneous volatility assumptions, creating systematic pricing errors that increase as correlation decreases.

nodes.title: Joint News, Attention Spillover,and Stock Returns

nodes.name: attention spillover overvaluation
nodes.description: Joint news coverage of multiple stocks triggers attention contagion via information search and social proof, causing temporary overvaluation of affected stocks that subsequently reverses. Investors' heightened attention to jointly-covered stocks inflates their valuations above fundamental levels.

nodes.name: post-attention-spillover reversal
nodes.description: Stocks experiencing joint news coverage and elevated attention exhibit contemporaneous price increases followed by predictable reversals as the attention-driven mispricing corrects. The temporary overvaluation created by attention contagion mean-reverts in subsequent periods.

nodes.name: marketwide attention-driven overvaluation
nodes.description: Aggregate joint news coverage across the market induces systematic overvaluation of the broader market, which subsequently corrects. This mechanism operates at the market level rather than individual stocks, with heightened joint news predicting negative future market returns.

nodes.title: Testing new property of elliptical model for stock returns distribution

nodes.name: elliptical distribution model violation
nodes.description: Stock returns in certain markets (e.g., China) violate the elliptical distribution assumption, creating exploitable mispricings when correlation structures deviate from expected elliptical properties. Traders can identify and exploit these deviations to generate alpha.

nodes.name: kendall correlation-sign coincidence decoupling
nodes.description: When the equality between Kendall's tau correlation coefficient and the probability of sign coincidence breaks down for stock pairs, it signals a violation of elliptical distribution assumptions, revealing mispriced correlation structures that can be exploited.

nodes.title: Stock returns forecast: an examination by means of Artificial Neural Networks

nodes.name: small-cap market inefficiency
nodes.description: Smaller stocks are less efficiently priced and thus exhibit greater predictability from historical price patterns, allowing neural networks to exploit autocorrelation in returns that larger, more liquid stocks eliminate through arbitrage.

nodes.name: return autocorrelation in illiquid markets
nodes.description: Past intraday returns contain predictive power for current returns in less-liquid small-cap stocks, suggesting that price adjustments lag information incorporation due to lower trading activity and market depth.

nodes.title: Empirical distributions of Chinese stock returns at different microscopic timescales

nodes.name: fat-tail distribution at short timescales
nodes.description: Return distributions exhibit progressively fatter power-law tails as timescale decreases toward single-trade intervals, indicating that extreme price movements are more frequent at microscopic timescales than traditional models predict. This creates exploitable mispricings when volatility clustering and tail risk are underestimated.

nodes.name: inverse cubic law at one-trade scale
nodes.description: Single-trade returns follow a strict inverse cubic power-law distribution, a distinct statistical regime that differs from the Student-t distributions observed at longer timescales. This structural break in the distribution function at the finest timescale reflects the microstructure mechanics of individual trade execution.

nodes.title: Inferring financial stock returns correlation from complex network analysis

nodes.name: correlation structure signal extraction
nodes.description: Stock returns exhibit meaningful collective behavior that can be distinguished from noise using eigenvalue decomposition of the correlation matrix. Stocks with high eigenvector centrality in the correlation network exhibit stronger collective modes that contain exploitable signal.

nodes.name: clustering-driven portfolio construction
nodes.description: Stocks that cluster together in the correlation network and exhibit high eigenvector centrality can be combined into portfolios that outperform traditional mean-variance optimization, particularly over short time horizons. The network structure of correlations contains information not captured by historical covariance matrices.

nodes.title: Weak Correlations of Stocks Future Returns

nodes.name: weak correlation mispricing
nodes.description: Assets exhibit pricing inefficiencies when their returns show weak correlations with explanatory variables, suggesting the market has not fully incorporated available information into valuations. Exploiting these correlation breakdowns allows construction of long-only portfolios that capture alpha.

nodes.title: Tail probabilities for short-term returns on stocks

nodes.name: tail probability scaling predictability
nodes.description: The tail probabilities of short-term returns scale predictably with measurement interval (power 3/2 relationship), creating exploitable patterns in extreme return events that reflect the inverse cubic decay of tail behavior across different time horizons.

nodes.title: Increasing market efficiency: Evolution of cross-correlations of stock returns

nodes.name: lead-lag correlation decay
nodes.description: Stock returns exhibit persistent lead-lag relationships where one stock's returns predictably precede another's, but these relationships have diminished over time as markets become more efficient and information disseminates faster across securities.

nodes.name: cross-correlation asymmetry reduction
nodes.description: Time-dependent cross-correlation functions between stocks exhibit asymmetry (peaks shifted away from zero lag) that reflects market microstructure frictions and slow information propagation, but this asymmetry decreases as markets evolve, indicating faster and more symmetric price discovery.

nodes.title: Variety of Stock Returns in Normal and Extreme Market Days: The August 1998 Crisis

nodes.name: market open return distribution shift
nodes.description: The distribution of stock returns undergoes sharp, localized changes at market open, creating temporary mispricings as the market reprices overnight information and order imbalances. This concentration of variety changes at the open allows traders to exploit predictable shifts in return distributions during the transition from closed to open market.

nodes.name: market close return distribution shift
nodes.description: The distribution of stock returns also exhibits localized changes at market close, though less pronounced than at open, as traders adjust positions and information is incorporated before market closure. This creates exploitable mispricings during the final trading period.

nodes.name: extreme volatility regime mispricing
nodes.description: During crisis periods like the August 1998 crash, heightened volatility and rapid changes in return distributions create temporary mispricings that persist longer than in normal market conditions. The breakdown of normal pricing relationships during extreme market days allows exploitation of these dislocations.

nodes.title: Capturing dynamics of post-earnings-announcement drift using genetic algorithm-optimised supervised learning

nodes.name: sector-specific earnings underreaction
nodes.description: Stock prices drift in the direction of earnings surprises at different speeds depending on the industrial sector, suggesting that market participants underreact to earnings news in a sector-dependent manner. Different sectors have different information processing speeds or risk factor sensitivities that cause the drift direction to be driven by different factors across sectors.

nodes.name: temporal earnings underreaction
nodes.description: The market's reaction to earnings announcements varies systematically across different quarters, with drift direction and magnitude driven by different factors at different times of year. This suggests seasonal or time-dependent patterns in how quickly investors process and incorporate earnings information into prices.

nodes.name: multi-factor earnings drift dynamics
nodes.description: Post-earnings-announcement drift is driven by a complex interaction of numerous fundamental and technical factors rather than a small set of variables, and the relative importance of these factors changes across stocks, sectors, and time periods. Traditional single or few-factor models miss the nuanced dynamics that machine learning can capture.

nodes.title: Investor Emotions and Earnings Announcements

nodes.name: pre-announcement sentiment overoptimism
nodes.description: Elevated investor excitement on social media prior to earnings announcements reflects overoptimistic expectations that are not justified by actual earnings outcomes, causing announcement returns to be lower than the sentiment would predict.

nodes.name: sentiment-earnings expectation divergence
nodes.description: Investor emotional enthusiasm predicts which firms will beat earnings expectations, but this predictive power of sentiment does not translate into positive returns because the market has already priced in the optimism, leaving no alpha for announcement day.

nodes.title: How do managers' non-responses during earnings calls affect analyst forecasts

nodes.name: information avoidance increases analyst uncertainty
nodes.description: Managers' non-responses during earnings calls reduce information clarity, causing analysts to face higher forecast errors and greater dispersion in their predictions due to unresolved uncertainty about firm fundamentals.

nodes.name: post-earnings drift from mispricing
nodes.description: Higher manager non-responses lead to delayed market incorporation of earnings information, as investors and analysts struggle to process ambiguous guidance, creating predictable post-announcement price drift.

nodes.name: information processing friction increases volatility
nodes.description: Manager non-responses raise the cognitive and informational costs for market participants to interpret earnings, leading to higher return volatility, wider bid-ask spreads, and increased trading volume as uncertainty persists.

nodes.title: Media abnormal tone, earnings announcements, and the stock market

nodes.name: media sentiment information lag
nodes.description: Media articles surrounding earnings announcements contain incremental sentiment information beyond what is disclosed in official earnings press releases and earnings calls. This information is not immediately priced in, allowing traders to exploit the delayed incorporation of media tone into stock prices.

nodes.name: abnormal tone price discovery friction
nodes.description: Abnormal (unexpected) shifts in media tone around earnings events reveal mispricings because market participants do not fully or immediately incorporate sentiment signals from media coverage into price discovery, creating exploitable gaps between sentiment and valuation.

nodes.title: Interpreting the Caste-based Earning Gaps in the Indian Labour Market: Theil and Oaxaca Decomposition Analysis
Predicting Stock Price Direction on Earnings Announcement Days using Multi-modal Deep Learning

nodes.name: pre-announcement sentiment predictability
nodes.description: News sentiment in the period before earnings announcements contains information about subsequent price direction on announcement day, suggesting that market participants do not fully incorporate available sentiment signals into prices before the announcement.

nodes.name: fundamental-technical-sentiment integration
nodes.description: The joint combination of firm fundamentals, technical price dynamics, and news sentiment provides predictive power for earnings announcement day returns that exceeds any single information source alone, indicating that markets incompletely integrate heterogeneous information types.

nodes.name: volatility clustering around announcements
nodes.description: Earnings announcements generate price discontinuities and elevated volatility that can be partially predicted from pre-announcement market dynamics and sentiment, suggesting that announcement-driven volatility is not purely exogenous but partially forecastable from prior information.

nodes.title: Heterogeneous Earnings Effects of the Job Corps by Gender Earnings: A Translated Quantile Approach
"Rich-Get-Richer"? Platform Attention and Earnings Inequality using Patreon Earnings Data

nodes.name: algorithmic attention concentration
nodes.description: Platform recommendation algorithms systematically direct disproportionate attention and earnings toward top creators, creating a self-reinforcing dynamic where initial success attracts further algorithmic promotion and user engagement.

nodes.name: rich-get-richer compounding effect
nodes.description: Earnings concentration follows a power-law distribution (Pareto exponent α≈2) where top earners capture disproportionate gains over time, with compounding returns to attention creating increasingly unequal wealth distribution across creators.

nodes.name: middle-class earnings displacement
nodes.description: When algorithmic attention shifts toward top creators, the earnings gains are drawn disproportionately from mid-tier creators rather than distributed evenly, causing the creator middle class to lose relative income share.

nodes.title: Bank Earnings, Credit Supply & the Macroeconomy: Evidence from Canada

nodes.name: bank net-worth credit supply expansion
nodes.description: Positive shocks to bank earnings expand intermediary net worth, which increases credit supply capacity and lowers corporate borrowing spreads. This mechanism links bank balance-sheet health directly to the cost and availability of credit in the broader economy.

nodes.name: corporate spread compression from credit supply
nodes.description: When banks experience positive earnings shocks that expand credit supply, corporate bond spreads compress as borrowing becomes cheaper and more available. This is the observable financial-market manifestation of improved intermediary net worth.

nodes.name: underreaction to bank earnings macroeconomic information
nodes.description: Market participants initially misprice bank earnings announcements by failing to fully incorporate their implications for credit conditions and real economic activity. This creates a predictive relationship where purged bank earnings news predicts subsequent movements in equity valuations, currency appreciation, and macroeconomic outcomes.

nodes.title: Quantitative earnings enhancement from share buybacks

nodes.name: market underestimation of buyback EPS accretion
nodes.description: The market systematically underestimates the positive mechanical effect of share buybacks on earnings per share, failing to fully price in the reduction in share count relative to the reduction in net earnings. This mispricing creates alpha as the market eventually corrects its valuation.

nodes.name: buyback price sensitivity of EPS accretion
nodes.description: The magnitude of EPS accretion from buybacks is highly sensitive to the price at which shares are repurchased. Buybacks executed at lower prices create greater accretion, but the market may not fully adjust expectations when the repurchase price changes, creating a mispriceable signal.

nodes.title: Earnings Prediction Using Recurrent Neural Networks

nodes.name: analyst coverage gap exploitation
nodes.description: Financial analysts provide incomplete coverage of firms and exhibit systematic biases in their forecasts. An RNN model that predicts earnings more accurately than analysts can identify mispriced securities where market prices have not yet incorporated superior earnings forecasts.

nodes.title: U.S. Long-Term Earnings Outcomes by Sex, Race, Ethnicity, and Place of Birth
Asymmetric response to PMI announcements in China's stock returns

nodes.name: information leakage ahead of macroeconomic announcements
nodes.description: Positive PMI news causes stock price increases 1 day before the official announcement and lasting ~3 days, suggesting market participants have advance knowledge of the announcement, generating predictable pre-announcement drift.

nodes.name: asymmetric reaction to positive vs negative news
nodes.description: Markets overreact to positive PMI announcements with sustained price increases, but underreact to negative PMI announcements with little to no price response, reflecting behavioral bias toward optimistic signals in a retail-dominated market.

nodes.name: risk-on bias in retail-dominated markets
nodes.description: China's stock market exhibits a structural preference for risk exposure due to the dominance of individual investors, causing sustained positive reactions to positive economic signals even when fundamentals do not justify the magnitude of the move.

nodes.name: institutional ownership dampening of negative news
nodes.description: Stocks with low institutional ownership exhibit stronger negative reactions to negative PMI news during downturns, suggesting institutional investors provide stabilizing demand that retail-heavy stocks lack.

nodes.title: The (Short-Term) Effects of Large Language Models on Unemployment and Earnings

nodes.name: LLM exposure earnings differential
nodes.description: Workers in occupations with high LLM exposure experience earnings increases post-ChatGPT adoption, while low-exposure occupations do not. Investors can exploit this differential earnings impact across sectors by identifying which occupations benefit from LLM productivity gains.

nodes.name: labor market adjustment through earnings rather than employment
nodes.description: LLM adoption causes short-term labor market adjustments primarily through earnings changes rather than unemployment or worker reallocation. This suggests wage pressure in exposed occupations without corresponding job losses, creating a mismatch between earnings growth and employment stability.

nodes.title: Heterogeneous Effects of Job Displacement on Earnings
Credit Information in Earnings Calls

nodes.name: credit information underreaction in earnings calls
nodes.description: Investors fail to fully internalize credit-relevant information disclosed in quarterly earnings call transcripts, leaving predictable patterns in credit spreads and firm profitability that can be exploited through text-based signals.

nodes.name: complexity-driven information neglect
nodes.description: As firm and earnings call complexity increases, investors are less likely to process and incorporate credit-relevant information from calls, making the text-based signal more predictive of future credit spreads and returns.

nodes.title: Corporate Earnings Calls and Analyst Beliefs

nodes.name: analyst overreaction to optimistic sentiment
nodes.description: Analysts systematically overweight positive sentiment in earnings call narratives relative to quantitative fundamentals, leading to inflated earnings expectations that subsequently correct downward as the market reprices.

nodes.name: analyst underreaction to risk narratives
nodes.description: Analysts systematically underweight risk and uncertainty narratives in earnings calls despite their predictive power for realized earnings, causing expectations to be too optimistic and vulnerable to downward revisions when risks materialize.

nodes.title: Detection of Accounting Anomalies in the Latent Space using Adversarial Autoencoder Neural Networks

nodes.name: undetected accounting fraud mispricing
nodes.description: Securities become mispriced when accounting irregularities and fraud go undetected by traditional auditing methods, allowing informed investors to exploit the eventual correction when fraud is discovered or becomes apparent.

nodes.name: reconstruction error anomaly detection
nodes.description: Adversarial autoencoders learn a latent representation of normal journal entry patterns; deviations from this learned representation (measured as reconstruction error) signal accounting anomalies that may indicate fraud or irregularities not caught by rule-based systems.

nodes.title: The Rise of Negative Earnings and Demand Shifting Investment

nodes.name: underreaction to negative earnings persistence
nodes.description: The market fails to fully account for the long-term implications of firms with rising negative earnings and increasing year-to-year loss persistence, leading to mispriced securities as investors underestimate the duration and severity of poor firm performance.

nodes.name: demand-shifting investment mispricing
nodes.description: Investors misprice firms that are shifting spending away from production costs toward sales, general, and administrative expenses, failing to recognize that this recomposition signals a fundamental change in business model and demand structure that impacts long-term profitability.

nodes.title: On the rate of convergence of estimating the Hurst parameter of rough stochastic volatility models
Estimating the Potential Impact of Combined Race and Ethnicity Reporting on Long-Term Earnings Statistics
Male Earnings Volatility in LEHD before, during, and after the Great Recession

nodes.name: labor market stability signal
nodes.description: Declining male earnings volatility (outside recessions) reflects improving labor market stability and reduced idiosyncratic worker risk, which investors can exploit by positioning in consumer-sensitive and economically-cyclical sectors that benefit from more predictable household income.

nodes.title: Reconciling Trends in U.S. Male Earnings Volatility: Results from Survey and Administrative Data
A growth adjusted price-earnings ratio

nodes.name: growth-adjusted valuation mispricing
nodes.description: The market misprices stocks by using traditional P/E ratios that ignore earnings growth, causing it to undervalue high-growth stocks with low payback periods adjusted for growth. Low GA-P/E stocks are systematically undervalued relative to their fundamental value when growth is properly accounted for.

nodes.title: Policy Expectation Counts? The Impact of China's Delayed Retirement Announcement on Urban Households Savings Rates

nodes.name: policy-driven precautionary savings shift
nodes.description: Households increase savings rates in response to delayed retirement policy announcements due to negative expectations about future pension income adequacy. This behavioral shift reduces current consumption and increases capital available for investment.

nodes.name: market underestimation of policy consumption impact
nodes.description: Financial markets underestimate the magnitude and speed of consumer behavior changes induced by policy announcements, creating a lag between the policy signal and full market repricing of consumption and savings dynamics.

nodes.title: Skill vs Education Types of Labour Mismatch and Their Association with Earnings
Platform Design, Earnings Transparency and Minimum Wage Policies: Evidence from A Natural Experiment on Lyft

nodes.name: earnings guarantee supply response
nodes.description: A minimum earnings guarantee reduces driver income uncertainty and increases the expected value of working, causing drivers to increase labor supply (working hours and utilization), which improves platform ride completion and availability.

nodes.name: transparency-induced strategic behavior
nodes.description: Enhanced per-ride earnings visibility allows drivers to make more informed decisions about which rides to accept and when to work, enabling them to optimize their effort allocation and potentially cherry-pick higher-paying opportunities, amplifying the supply response.

nodes.name: supply-demand positive spillover
nodes.description: Increased driver supply (from the guarantee and transparency) reduces rider wait times and improves service quality, which generates positive externalities that increase rider demand and platform utilization.

nodes.title: Eco-Innovation and Earnings Management: Unveiling the Moderating Effects of Financial Constraints and Opacity in FTSE All-Share Firms

nodes.name: earnings management under financial constraints
nodes.description: Firms facing financial constraints use earnings management (income smoothing) to project financial stability and meet stakeholder expectations, masking their true financial health. This behavior is amplified in constrained firms pursuing eco-innovation.

nodes.name: eco-innovation as earnings management cover
nodes.description: Firms leverage eco-innovation announcements and investments as a strategic cover for earnings management activities, allowing them to signal sustainability commitment while simultaneously manipulating reported financial performance.

nodes.name: opacity-driven mispricing
nodes.description: High financial opacity in constrained firms pursuing eco-innovation creates information asymmetry that leads to systematic mispricing of their true financial health and sustainability commitments, enabling informed investors to exploit the gap between reported and actual performance.

nodes.title: Volatility jumps and the classification of monetary policy announcements

nodes.name: volatility jump classification signal
nodes.description: Monetary policy announcements produce predictable, isolated volatility jumps that can be classified and exploited in the immediate post-announcement window before noise from concurrent events contaminates the signal. Traders can generate alpha by identifying and trading on these announcement-specific volatility shifts.

nodes.title: On Classifying the Effects of Policy Announcements on Volatility

nodes.name: central bank announcement volatility regime shift
nodes.description: Central bank policy announcements trigger discrete shifts in market volatility regimes (increases, decreases, or no effect). Traders can exploit mispricings by accurately predicting which regime an announcement will induce, positioning ahead of the volatility adjustment.

nodes.title: Should I Stay or Should I Go Now? An Investigation into Gender Differences in the Impact of Switching Jobs on Earnings
A Stock Selection Method Based on Earning Yield Forecast Using Sequence Prediction Models

nodes.name: fundamental value mispricing from earnings prediction
nodes.description: Market participants systematically misprice stocks because they fail to accurately forecast future earning yields (EBIT/EV). Machine learning models that better capture temporal patterns in historical earnings data can predict intrinsic value more accurately than traditional methods, allowing investors to exploit the gap between market price and true fundamental value.

nodes.title: The Effect of High-Speed Rail Connectivity on Capital Market Earnings Forecast Error: Evidence from the Chinese Stock Market

nodes.name: information friction reduction via geographic accessibility
nodes.description: High-speed rail connectivity reduces the travel costs and time required for analysts to conduct in-person due diligence (plant visits, management meetings), enabling them to gather soft information more efficiently and update earnings forecasts with greater accuracy.

nodes.name: forecast accuracy lag exploitation
nodes.description: Analysts' earnings forecast errors decline following HSR connectivity, but the market adjusts to this improved information with a lag, creating a window where investors can exploit mispriced stocks before consensus expectations fully incorporate the enhanced forecast accuracy.

nodes.title: Bayesian Forecasting of Stock Returns on the JSE using Simultaneous Graphical Dynamic Linear Models

nodes.name: cross-series dependency forecasting
nodes.description: Stock returns are predictable by capturing interrelationships and dependencies among multiple stocks in a multivariate system, rather than forecasting each stock in isolation. The causal mechanism is that correlated price movements across stocks contain information that improves return forecasts when properly modeled.

nodes.name: market gyration responsiveness
nodes.description: Bayesian dynamic models that recalibrate their parameters in real-time can respond more quickly and accurately to sudden market fluctuations and regime changes than static models, generating alpha through superior timing during volatile periods.

nodes.title: Forecasting stock return distributions around the globe with quantile neural networks

nodes.name: non-Gaussian distribution forecasting alpha
nodes.description: Traditional models assume Gaussian return distributions and miss fat tails and asymmetries; more accurate forecasts of these higher-order moments enable better risk management and trading decisions, generating alpha through superior prediction of extreme outcomes.

nodes.name: mean-variance forecast improvement
nodes.description: The quantile neural network produces more accurate out-of-sample forecasts of mean and variance compared to standard models; these improved predictions allow traders to better estimate expected returns and volatility, reducing mispricing.

nodes.title: The Value of Information from Sell-side Analysts

nodes.name: delayed analyst interpretation of earnings
nodes.description: Market participants underreact to earnings announcements because sell-side analysts' qualitative interpretations of income statement data take time to disseminate and be incorporated into prices. Early access to analyst reports allows traders to profit from this lag before the market fully prices in the nuanced financial insights.

nodes.name: income statement analysis information premium
nodes.description: Analysts' detailed qualitative analyses of income statements contain economically significant information about future returns that is not immediately reflected in prices. This analysis accounts for more than half of the explanatory power of analyst reports, suggesting the market systematically undervalues this interpretive work relative to raw quantitative forecasts.

nodes.title: Using Machine Learning to Forecast Future Earnings

nodes.name: ML-superior earnings forecasting
nodes.description: Machine learning models capture complex nonlinear patterns in financial data that traditional statistical methods and analyst consensus miss, enabling more accurate earnings predictions ahead of market consensus and generating alpha through information advantage.

nodes.title: Transfer Ranking in Finance: Applications to Cross-Sectional Momentum with Data Scarcity

nodes.name: cross-sectional momentum signal extraction
nodes.description: Assets exhibit predictable relative performance patterns that can be captured by ranking instruments based on their recent price momentum. The self-attention mechanism identifies complex interactions among assets to refine these rankings, improving signal quality beyond simple historical returns.

nodes.name: transfer learning generalization
nodes.description: Models trained on data-scarce target datasets overfit and degrade in performance. By fusing encoder representations from a larger source dataset with similar characteristics, the model learns more robust feature representations that generalize better to out-of-sample target data.

nodes.title: An Equilibrium Model for the Cross-Section of Liquidity Premia

nodes.name: liquidity premium misalignment
nodes.description: Assets earn a liquidity premium proportional to their transaction costs in equilibrium. When observed liquidity premia deviate from the equilibrium relationship with transaction costs, assets become mispriced and exploitable.

nodes.name: transaction cost capitalization
nodes.description: Transaction costs are priced into equilibrium asset returns through a risk-sharing mechanism where heterogeneous agents adjust their trading strategies and demand based on the costs they face. Higher transaction costs lead to higher required returns.

nodes.title: Building Cross-Sectional Systematic Strategies By Learning to Rank

nodes.name: ranking accuracy improvement via learning-to-rank
nodes.description: Machine learning algorithms that learn pairwise and listwise relationships among assets produce more accurate asset rankings than traditional heuristic or regression-based sorting methods, leading to better portfolio construction and higher risk-adjusted returns.

nodes.name: cross-sectional momentum
nodes.description: Assets with stronger recent relative performance (higher momentum scores) are ranked higher and overweighted in portfolios, exploiting the persistence of cross-sectional return differences.

nodes.title: Implicit Bias against a Capitalistic Society Predicts Market Earnings

nodes.name: ideological bias dampening profit expectations
nodes.description: Individuals with stronger implicit bias against capitalism form lower expectations about their earning potential, leading them to set conservative profit targets and underperform in trading. This behavioral suppression of ambition directly reduces realized profits independent of market conditions.

nodes.name: contrarian exploitation of biased trading behavior
nodes.description: Investors with ideological bias against capitalism systematically underperform due to conservative trading strategies and low profit targets. Contrarian investors can exploit this predictable underperformance by taking opposite positions against the biased traders' conservative behavior.

nodes.title: ChatGPT and the Labor Market: Unraveling the Effect of AI Discussions on Students' Earnings Expectations

nodes.name: sentiment-driven earnings expectation revision
nodes.description: Negative AI discussion sentiment causes students to downwardly revise their earnings expectations, which propagates into reduced consumer confidence and altered investment decisions in labor-market-sensitive sectors.

nodes.name: differential vulnerability belief updating
nodes.description: Non-STEM and non-male student subgroups exhibit asymmetric pessimistic belief updates about AI labor market impact relative to STEM majors, creating heterogeneous shifts in sector-specific demand expectations that may drive mispricing in education and AI-disruption-sensitive equities.

nodes.title: Optimal Investment Strategy to Minimize Occupation Time

nodes.name: downside risk minimization through dynamic allocation
nodes.description: An investor dynamically rebalances between riskless and risky assets to minimize the expected duration of negative wealth states. By optimizing the timing and magnitude of risky asset exposure, the strategy reduces occupation time in drawdown regimes, generating alpha through superior downside management.

nodes.name: consumption-smoothing driven rebalancing
nodes.description: An investor maintaining constant consumption while managing wealth dynamics must adjust asset allocation to sustain consumption through volatile periods. This creates a systematic rebalancing signal that tilts away from risky assets as wealth approaches zero, reducing the probability and duration of ruin.

nodes.title: The Circle of Investment: Connecting the Dots of the Portfolio Management Cycle...

nodes.name: portfolio drift correction through rebalancing
nodes.description: Portfolio returns deviate from target asset allocation over time due to differential asset performance. Systematic rebalancing back to intended weights captures alpha by enforcing disciplined buy-low/sell-high behavior and maintaining risk parameters.

nodes.name: risk-adjusted hypothesis refinement
nodes.description: Investment hypotheses contain inherent ambiguity and measurement error. Iteratively refining these hypotheses through performance measurement and risk management feedback loops reduces decision-making uncertainty and improves strategy alignment, generating alpha through better calibration.

nodes.title: Endogenous Representation of Asset Returns

nodes.name: endogenous network spillovers
nodes.description: Asset returns are partially explained by a sparse network of direct interactions among other assets rather than exogenous factors. Price movements propagate through this endogenous network structure, creating systematic risk that appears factor-like but originates from asset-to-asset dependencies.

nodes.name: mispricing from factor model misspecification
nodes.description: Traditional exogenous factor models misattribute endogenous asset interactions to external factors, causing systematic mispricing of assets whose true risk drivers are their connections within the asset network rather than conventional risk factors.

nodes.title: Digital Transformation and Corporate Financial Asset Allocation: Evidence from China

nodes.name: digital transformation investment efficiency
nodes.description: Firms undergoing digital transformation improve their information processing capabilities and investment decision-making, enabling them to allocate capital more efficiently toward higher-yielding financial assets and optimize asset maturity structures.

nodes.name: information efficiency improvement
nodes.description: Digital transformation enhances firms' ability to process and act on information, reducing information asymmetries and curbing inefficient capital allocation decisions that would otherwise persist.

nodes.name: expanded investment opportunity set
nodes.description: Digitalization broadens the range of financial instruments and investment avenues available to firms, allowing them to access previously unavailable long-term high-yield assets and diversify their financial asset portfolios.

nodes.title: Optimal Investment Strategy for Risky Assets

nodes.name: long-term growth rate optimization
nodes.description: Investors can generate alpha by dynamically allocating capital to risky assets based on their return-volatility tradeoff to maximize long-term compounded growth, rather than following static mean-variance optimization. This mechanism exploits the fact that multiplicative (log-normal) asset dynamics reward volatility differently than additive Gaussian frameworks.

nodes.name: volatility-adjusted capital allocation
nodes.description: The optimal fraction of capital allocated to risky assets depends on both average return and volatility; high-volatility assets require proportionally lower allocation weights to maximize long-term growth, even if expected returns are attractive. This corrects for the failure of traditional portfolio theories in very risky asset regimes.

nodes.title: Auctioning Corporate Bonds: A Uniform-Price under Investment Mandates

nodes.name: risk mandate constraint on bidding
nodes.description: Investors with tighter risk limits (lower risk tolerance) submit lower bids in uniform-price auctions, reducing their demand pressure. This constraint mechanically depresses equilibrium yields and can lead to bond underpricing when risk mandates are loose across the bidder pool.

nodes.name: mandate-driven demand heterogeneity
nodes.description: Heterogeneous risk limits across institutional investors create differential bidding strategies in the auction. Investors with high risk tolerance bid more aggressively, while those with tight constraints bid conservatively, fragmenting demand and affecting the equilibrium price discovery process.

nodes.name: auction mechanism information revelation
